Is stretching good for health or a waste of time?

It depends. Can you put your hand flat on the floor from a standing position?

If no, you need to stretch.
It looks like I need to stretch.
For me it makes all the difference in the world, but I'm competitive about it. No pushing to achieve weird poses. Do it gently for a year and you'll get wherever you need to get to.
I have tight calves. If I don't stretch them several times daily, I will end up with stress fractures. So keep those calves stretched otherwise you spend your summer in a walking boot
I hear old people say they wish they had started earlier.

Stretching is good for your health. It loosens up your muscles, preventing soreness and injuries. It also feels amazing. Try to stretch every day, if you can. Also look into the difference between dynamic and static stretching!
Especially if it is done for you by a big titted professional massage therapist.

I'm 50, quality of life is better if I start the day with some stretching. General aches and pains are less, I have more energy, and I can move more easily. Is it good for my health? I don't know but I feel better.

Its good but doesn't help anything before exercise. In fact I think static stretching was shown to cause more injuries, especially in athletes that need stability like weightlifters. So do it after exercise or just whenever.

I'm at the brink of forty, and let me tell you, thank god for stretching.

Been doing it regularly since my 20s, and my body is more loose, flexible, and over all useful than most people I know. I work with guys 10 years younger than me that walk around like old men, creaky and stiff. I'm nearly always loose with a bit of a spring in my step, and I know it's from stretching because if I don't have time for a good stretch for more than a day, I feel tight and gross.

Plus, I try to stay pretty physical, yet I never have any significant pulled or strained muscles, so there's that too. Fully recommend it.
Improves flexibility and consequently agility. Also hugely reduces soreness, which in turn hugely increases motivation to work out the next day. You have not experienced this for yourself?
